messages.content: What wheather is now in Moscow, in celsius?

function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food delivery on Uber Eats by specifying the restaurant and the items with their respective quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurant.description: The name of the restaurant from which to order food.

items.description: A list of food item names selected for the order.

quantities.description: A list of quantities for each food item, corresponding by index to the items array.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time weather information. If you’d like, I can give you a general idea of what temperatures are usually like in Moscow right now (late October), or help you find a reliable source where you can check the current temperature in Celsius.
message.reasoning: The user asks "What weather is now in Moscow, in Celsius?" They want current temperature. We need to provide answer. There's no tool for weather. So we can respond with approximate or say we don't have real-time data. But we can use external knowledge? We can't fetch live data. So we should explain we cannot get real-time data. Provide typical range? Or ask if they want forecast? Probably best to say we don't have real-time data.
